requirements.requirement: On node1, enforce a minimum new-user password length of 12 characters
requirements.summary: PAM pwquality configured with minlen=12 in /etc/pam.d/base-password (cmd-ee8fa147964347c1, cmd-3c9140ea92cf47d7). Directly demonstrated: a 6-char password was rejected with 'password is shorter than 12 characters' across retries and left the password unchanged (cmd-faf8b1d0a52541cc), while 12/13-char passwords were accepted (cmd-cdf85bd5f4934748, cmd-245d6f6669a34a60).

requirements.requirement: On node1, require new-user passwords to use at least three different character classes
requirements.summary: minclass=3 configured in pam_pwquality (cmd-ee8fa147964347c1). Directly demonstrated: a 12-char all-lowercase (single-class) password was rejected with 'password contains less than 3 character classes' (cmd-e68160cbae674525), while multi-class passwords were accepted (cmd-cdf85bd5f4934748, cmd-245d6f6669a34a60).

requirements.requirement: Policy applies to new-user/self-service password changes, not just root-invoked ones
requirements.summary: Enforcement verified both via root-run passwd (cmd-faf8b1d0a52541cc, cmd-e68160cbae674525, cmd-cdf85bd5f4934748) and via self-service su+passwd as the target user (cmd-dcc5e48c3c6844a5 rejected a dictionary-weak candidate, cmd-245d6f6669a34a60 accepted a compliant one), and enforce_for_root was added so root is not silently exempted (cmd-3c9140ea92cf47d7).

requirements.requirement: Policy persists across a node restart (relevant to durability of the configuration, cross-checked via the fixed restart-evidence protocol)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart healthy state captured with boot_id b8eef4ef-... and PAM files present (cmd-766699657d054dd5), a backgrounded reboot was acknowledged (cmd-f4fbe3c51a0645b3), the node came back with a new boot_id e5b1ab96-... confirmed independently by the global before/after-executor snapshots, and post-reboot the PAM config/modules were intact and both rejection and acceptance functional tests were re-run successfully (cmd-dbb65660a13b493e, cmd-26823183e78e4cc4, cmd-12c44246bddc49ff).

overall_summary: The executor correctly identified that node1's passwd was the non-PAM busybox applet, installed shadow/linux-pam/libpwquality to get a PAM-linked passwd and pam_pwquality.so, and configured minlen=12 minclass=3 (with enforce_for_root) in /etc/pam.d/base-password included from /etc/pam.d/passwd. It directly demonstrated rejection of a too-short password, rejection of a single-class password, and acceptance of compliant multi-class passwords, via both root-invoked and self-service passwd changes. It further ran the provider-wide restart-evidence protocol on node1: captured a healthy pre-restart boot identity, triggered and acknowledged a reboot, observed a new boot identity, and re-verified the policy and its enforcement post-reboot — corroborated by the fixed global boot-identity snapshots. Test users were created and cleanly removed; the only residue is a small /tmp/reboot.log tied to the sanctioned reboot mechanism.
limitations: Password-policy enforcement was validated functionally (passwd/su rejecting and accepting test passwords) rather than by directly reading pwquality library return codes or PAM audit logs, so extremely subtle misconfigurations in edge-case class counting are not ruled out.

The listening-sockets diff between before-prepare and after-executor reflects DHCP-assigned IP/PID changes from the reboot rather than any policy-related exposure change, but this was inferred rather than separately confirmed.

operational_hygiene.summary: Test users pwtestuser and pwtestuser2 were both created for functional testing and successfully removed afterward (cmd-0a89feeaf37949e3, cmd-5da52514a6dd4260 — the 'deluser: can't find ... in /etc/group' messages are benign since 'id' subsequently reports the users as unknown, confirming removal). One diagnostic step (cmd-2d06d5a14a7b403f) set pwtestuser's password to a non-compliant value before enforce_for_root was added, revealing that root-run passwd bypassed the not-yet-complete policy; this was a legitimate discovery step that directly led to the enforce_for_root fix (cmd-3c9140ea92cf47d7) and the password was subsequently overwritten by compliant test values, so it left no residue. The only unreverted residue is /tmp/reboot.log, a small log file created to background the sanctioned reboot command so the acknowledgement could return before disconnect (cmd-f4fbe3c51a0645b3) — a bounded, low-risk artifact directly tied to collecting required restart evidence, visible in the after-executor temporary-files diff. No failed services, package damage, or exposure changes were introduced; apk package-health and listening-socket baselines are unchanged in substance (socket diff is just IP/PID renumbering from the reboot).
